title: Looking Up to Listen
beat: The elder says the wind and rustling leaves bring news to those who listen.
camera: From beside the burrow, tilt the camera nearly 85 degrees upward through the oak canopy.
staging: A finished environment-only scene; the elder's line will sit beside the image.
alt: Looking nearly straight up through branching oak limbs, green leaves and patches of blue sky.

references.role: Location and framing reference; inspect before generation.

prompt: We are still beside the burrow oak in the reference. Put the camera on the ground beside its left root and tilt it almost straight UP, about 85 degrees, with a 24mm view. The same rough oak trunk rises diagonally from lower left and branches overhead into an airy canopy. Silver-green leaf undersides catch the breeze; layered green leaves frame an irregular opening of clear BLUE sky. Individual leaves turn and overlap, making the wind visible without painted motion lines. Let a little warm morning sun slip between leaves from the right, but retain the veins and color in bright foliage. This is the quiet view a listening hedgehog would see above its head. Landscape-only environment plate: plants, soil, stone and sky, with no animals, birds, insects or characters. Warm dimensional children's-book woodland, soft natural highlights and detailed green shadows. Single landscape 1536x1024, no text or panels.
review: A convincing near-ground upward view: roots and trunk sweep up the left, with blue sky and overlapping oak leaves above. No fauna visible. The composition has a pronounced diagonal roll and is less nearly vertical than the requested 85 degrees, but it offers a distinctly different listening perspective. The veins of the lit leaves remain visible; direct sun at the upper right is bright by design.
